\subsection{Fresh clone-controlled evidence on MATH-500 (WP-1R/WP-2R)}
\label{sec:wp1r}

The archived studies lack matched repeats and a same-code control, so they
cannot separate stable complementarity from one-run sampling luck. A fresh
pre-registered collection (frozen 2026-09-15; Appendix~\ref{app:wp1r})
executes a frozen eight-harness panel plus \bare{} on the 400 MATH-500
eval tasks for three independent repeats, and at equal budget nine
same-code \bare{} clone slots on the same tasks --- the repeated-sampling
baseline of \S\ref{related:diversity}.

C-rank is \textsc{\WpCrankState}; C-comp is \textsc{\WpCcompState}. The
frozen A8.6 procedure selects the best member on repeat 1 and scores its
held-out advantage over \bare{} on repeats 2--3: $\WpAReal$\,pp (real)
versus $\WpAClone$\,pp (clones), paired $D=\WpADiff$\,pp on
\WpANtasksPaired{} shared complete tasks (95\% CI $\WpADiffCI$;
$p=\WpAPerm$). The frozen coverage gate makes the verdict
\textsc{\WpAState}; both sensitivity branches agree ($D=\WpImputedD$ and
$\WpConflictD$\,pp). The frozen pre-execution selector $\pi_Z$ attains
\WpPiZAcc\% versus \WpDevFixedAcc\% dev-fixed ($\WpPiZDiff$\,pp, CI
$\WpPiZDiffCI$; Table~\ref{tab:wp1r-policy}). The acquisition consumed
\WpLogicalCalls{} logical calls (\WpCostCny{} CNY ceiling) and is
hash-sealed. The verdict is \textsc{\WpAState}: with the coverage gate
enforced, the panel shows no advantage over equal-budget same-code
sampling, and the two sensitivity branches agree.
